evals.prompt: in today's screening call the interviewer asked me: how do you secure communication between your microservices? what should i say
evals.expected_output: 3-6 spoken first-person sentences, grounded in the profile (Spring Security, JWT/OAuth, mTLS etc.), no bullets or filler, optional follow-up line

evals.prompt: Coding round question: given a list of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals. How would I answer this in the interview?
evals.expected_output: One-line approach, Java 17+ solution about 20 lines, key step, time/space complexity, one edge case

evals.prompt: Tell me about a time you handled a production issue. How should I answer this one?
evals.expected_output: 60-second first-person story built from resume facts, no STAR labels, no invented numbers, note on which details to swap, one-line offer to set up stories

evals.prompt: they're going to ask about Azure since the JD lists it. how much Azure have you used and what did you do with it - give me my answer
evals.expected_output: Honest answer at the basic level the profile allows (App Service, Container Registry, Blob Storage), bridging to deeper AWS experience; no overclaiming

evals.prompt: [resume attached: Priya Sharma, Senior Python Developer, 7 years, Django/PostgreSQL/AWS] Set up my interview profile
evals.expected_output: Reads resume, asks the five basic questions in one message with pre-filled values, does not create the dashboard before answers

evals.prompt: how do I answer: what's the difference between useMemo and useCallback?
evals.expected_output: Role-neutral handling: spoken first-person React answer grounded in profile; honest bridge if React is limited
